appraisal_events.evidence: « Allons, Monsieur Vallenères, faites la jeune fille », dit Mme de Villeparisis à l'archiviste, « selon une plaisanterie consacrée » ; l'archiviste s'exécute et présente l'assiette de petits fours.
appraisal_events.explanation: The hostess assigns her salaried archivist the feminized serving role of a daughter of the house through a joke the narrator marks as a fixed household ritual, and he silently complies by handing round the cakes. The narrator's tag « plaisanterie consacrée » ironizes the salon's stale wit while confirming Vallenères's standing position as its serviceable inferior.

appraisal_events.evidence: « dit M. d'Argencourt qui, par esprit d'imitation, reprit la plaisanterie de Mme de Villeparisis »
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly attributes d'Argencourt's sally to imitativeness rather than wit, so his one contribution to the conversation is framed as borrowed from the hostess. This lowers him rhetorically in the very act of his attempting to shine.

status_effects.explanation: Vallenères is locally placed below the guests: he is the standing butt of a house joke and performs the serving function, passing the plate on to another guest.
His witticism is narrated as mere echo of Mme de Villeparisis's, so he gains nothing and is exposed as rhetorically derivative.

She sets the tone of her salon: her formula governs the archivist's behaviour and is copied by a guest, which locally marks her as the room's rhetorical model even though the narrator finds the joke worn.

ambiguities: The referent of « Monsieur » in d'Argencourt's line is not stated: it most plausibly designates the archivist, who is actually performing the « rôle de jeune fille » by handing round the petits fours, but it could be read as aimed at M. de Guermantes, who has just spoken and accepted a baba — which would redirect the joke's target and make it a light tease of the duke instead.

Because the joke is « consacrée », it can be read either as a ritual mark of Vallenères's familiarity within the house (inclusion) or as the routine, unexamined subordination of a salaried dependent (diminishment); the passage supplies no reaction from him that would settle the sign.
